calibration_note: No bias correction applied, for the EIGHTH time, and the ratios were recomputed from estimates.jsonl and outcomes.jsonl in this session rather than recalled. Estimated-over-actual on ACTIVE quantity, all seven: scaffolding 2.27x over (n=1); data-modelling 0.48x, i.e. UNDER by 2.10x (n=1); llm-integration 0.80x, UNDER by 1.24x (n=1); agent-implementation 1.31x, 2.18x, 1.41x, 1.79x - four points, every one an over-estimate, mean 1.67x, geometric mean 1.64x, median 1.60x, standard deviation 0.40, coefficient of variation 0.24, range 1.31x to 2.18x. That is the whole corpus: seven outcomes, four classes, one class with more than a single point. THE IRONY IS EXPLICIT AND IT CHANGES NOTHING, which is the answer this estimate is being asked for. After OUT-0007 closed, agent-implementation stands at n = 4 - one short of the n = 5 threshold that BiasDetective, the component THIS PHASE BUILDS, will refuse below. The temptation is to treat building the thing as licence to pre-apply it. Four reasons that is wrong, in the order they matter. FIRST, the threshold is a fact about the sample and not about the calendar: n = 4 is n = 4 whether or not the code that would decline it exists yet, and a rule that bends in the phase that implements it was never a rule. Doing it here would be the first break in eight estimates, and it would land in the one phase whose entire purpose is to make the manual discipline and the code agree - the property tests written this phase are supposed to PROVE they agree, and they cannot prove it about an author who just made an exception for himself. SECOND, the dispersion argues against correcting even if the threshold were met, and this phase is where that stops being prose: the four ratios scatter from 1.31x to 2.18x with a coefficient of variation of 0.24, so a mean-fitted factor of 1.67x applied to 5.5h yields 3.3h while the sample's own range yields anywhere from 2.5h to 4.2h. That spread is over half the point estimate. Pricing this phase on the mean would commit, in the estimate itself, precisely the error the phase's own ADR is being written to reject - EST-0007 said a mean-only factor would have mispriced Phase 5, and that is the worked example scope item 1 names. THIRD, there is a real sub-population question that n = 4 cannot answer: all four prior agent-implementation phases built agents that CALL A MODEL, and this phase builds three that do not, which removes the largest single source of variance in phases 3 through 6 (model behaviour, prompt iteration, citation-gate starvation) and adds a different one (hypothesis finding counterexamples that force a design change). Splitting the class on that axis would leave n = 4 and n = 0. The honest move is to price that difference into CONFIDENCE, which is done - 0.50 rather than the 0.45 of the last four - and not into the quantity. FOURTH, the arrival matters more than the correction: when OUT-0008 closes, agent-implementation reaches n = 5 and EST-0009 becomes THE FIRST ESTIMATE IN THIS PROJECT'S HISTORY THAT BIASDETECTIVE CAN LEGITIMATELY SPEAK ABOUT. Phase 7 builds the component; Phase 8 is the first phase it can price. Arriving there with four clean uncorrected points is worth more to the Phase 12 demo than one tuned number is worth to this estimate. What IS applied, as in every phase since OUT-0005, is SCOPE correction, which is not a bias correction wearing a different hat: the conditions price components rather than phases, price the CLI as a line item, price the eval work as a module plus four edits, price each component's refusal vocabulary inside the component, and price the arithmetic/judgement boundary as its own subject - which in this phase falls between computing a factor and deciding whether to speak it, not between a model call and the maths around it.
risk_note: Four risks, and the line count is not among them. FIRST and most likely: the output SHAPE, not the arithmetic. The arithmetic here is a geometric mean and a log-space spread over at most a few dozen rows and it is not where a day goes. Where a day goes is discovering, after BiasDetective is written and tested, that Phase 8's fusion query - 'this team's factor for migration work is 1.8x under, n=14, confidence 0.79' - cannot be answered in one call without an expensive walk. Phase 1 paid this cost up front for the Link table and Phase 6 paid it for calibration_history, both times by executing the future query rather than sketching it. This estimate assumes the same is done BEFORE the shape is frozen, and prices it inside the BiasDetective line item. SECOND: the dispersion decision is a genuine design fork with three defensible answers - refuse when the spread is wide, widen the interval and still speak, or speak the central tendency and let the caller read the interval - and the wrong one is cheap to write and expensive to unpick, because CalibratorAgent, ScoringAgent, the eval harness and the Phase 8 query all read the result. It is settled in an ADR before the second component is written, not after. THIRD: a property test that passes because the generator never produces the interesting case. 'BiasDetective never emits below n = 5' is trivially satisfied by a strategy that never reaches n = 5, and 'a correction never yields a non-positive quantity' is trivially satisfied by a strategy that never produces a factor near zero. The hypothesis strategies have to be built to reach the boundary and the tests have to assert the boundary was reached - otherwise this phase's headline claim is unearned, and unlike a starved corpus number there is no honest excuse available for it. FOURTH: the ScoringAgent backtest against docs/dogfood is a trap worth naming before it is written. n = 7 across four classes, with the only multi-point class at n = 4, cannot support any claim at all; a backtest showing a correction 'would have helped' there is noise with a decimal point on it. It is reported as a curiosity, in those words, in the module docstring, in the phase report and beneath the table - or it is not reported.

conditions: MOST OF THE LINKING WORK IS ALREADY DONE AND IS NOT REPRICED. This is the single largest reason this estimate is smaller than the phase sounds

BiasDetective(repository).factor_for(owner=, work_class=) is the whole of it - executed in this session against docs/dogfood rather than read off the handover, returning verdict, factor, magnitude, low, high, n, considered, resolved, excluded, direction, reason and describe(). the four components are priced separately at roughly 380, 300, 250 and 300 production lines with test files at least as large, and each component's refusal vocabulary is priced INSIDE the component. Bought by OUT-0005, confirmed by OUT-0006, OUT-0007 and OUT-0008 - the most reliable correction in this record and the only structural one applied without argument. The boundary in this phase falls between recognition and evaluation - and the strong suspicion, priced in, is that recognition for the edges that ALREADY EXIST needs no model at all, because Phase 4 paid for the judgement when it wrote the edge. If that turns out to be impossible, this item is cut to the backlog with the reason written down and the phase still ships

calibration_note: A BIAS CORRECTION IS APPLIED, FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS PROJECT'S HISTORY. The previous eight estimates all refused, correctly, because no group had reached n=5. OUT-0008 took agent-implementation to exactly five, so this is the first estimate Praxis's own rule permits to be corrected, and refusing here would make MINIMUM_SAMPLE decorative - a threshold nobody crosses is not a threshold. RECOMPUTED IN THIS SESSION by running the shipped code (praxis.agents.bias.summarise over CalibrationRows built from estimates.jsonl and outcomes.jsonl) rather than copied from the Phase 7 handover. The five agent-implementation ratios, estimated-active over actual-active: EST-0004 5.5/4.2 = 1.3095, EST-0005 6.0/2.75 = 2.1818, EST-0006 6.5/4.6 = 1.4130, EST-0007 5.0/2.8 = 1.7857, EST-0008 5.5/2.1 = 2.6190. BiasDetective returns verdict=measured, factor=0.5556, magnitude=1.7999x over, band 0.4156 to 0.7429 (read as 1.35x to 2.41x over), n=5, considered=5, resolved=5, excluded=0, direction=over, confidence=0.3875. THE ARITHMETIC, both steps kept separate on purpose. Step one, the RAW estimate, built bottom-up from the line items in conditions by exactly the procedure the previous five agent-implementation estimates used - four components at roughly 380/300/250/300 production lines with tests at least as large, plus the CLI, plus the eval module and its four edits, plus two ADRs and the report - which lands at 6.5h, the same figure EST-0006 reached for a comparably sized phase and one hour above EST-0008's 5.5h because this phase has four components where Phase 7 had three. The procedure was deliberately NOT made more pessimistic before the factor was applied: the factor corrects THIS procedure, so changing the procedure and applying the correction would count the same adjustment twice. Step two, the CORRECTION: 6.5 x 0.5556 = 3.6114, logged as 3.6h. The band travels with it and is not dropped on the way to a headline number, which ADR 0024 made inseparable for exactly this reason: 6.5 x 0.7429 = 4.83h at the least-corrected end, 6.5 x 0.4156 = 2.70h at the most-corrected end. So the honest statement is 3.6h with a plausible range of 2.7h to 4.8h, and the five actuals this was fitted on were 4.2, 2.75, 4.6, 2.8 and 2.1 - mean 3.29h - which puts 3.6h just above the historical mean, where the largest-scope phase of the six belongs. WHETHER THE CLASSIFICATION IS HONEST, which is the harder question and is answered rather than dodged. agent-implementation is not a homogeneous class: it contains Phase 7, which called no model at all and came in 2.62x over, and Phase 5, which was a predicate DSL plus four agents and came in 1.41x over. That variance IS the sub-population problem and the band is wide because of it. Phase 8 is model-driven again - cross-document OutcomeMatcher calls a provider, and FusionBridge may - which makes EST-0009 a BETTER fit for this factor than Phase 7 was, since four of the five fitted phases were model-driven. Stated plainly: the factor is applied because this phase resembles the population it was fitted on more closely than the phase that produced the worst ratio in it. The alternative - splitting the class so that Phase 8 is compared only against model-driven phases - would drop n to 4 and silence the detective, and inventing a class boundary to escape a factor is the override ADR 0024 refuses to provide, arriving through a side door. The class stays; the concern is logged as a condition instead. WHAT THIS ESTIMATE DOES DIFFERENTLY FROM EST-0008, stated because the product owner asked for it explicitly. EST-0008's report named its own mistake: it correctly saw that Phase 7 was cheaper than its predecessors - five deterministic modules, no model calls - and expressed that insight by raising confidence from 0.45 to 0.50 while leaving active_quantity at 5.5h, unchanged. Wrong lever, and it cost 2.62x, the worst miss in the record. EST-0009 CORRECTS FOR IT rather than repeating it, and the correction is visible in the numbers: the entire adjustment this time is in the QUANTITY (6.5h raw becomes 3.6h logged, a 45% cut), and confidence moves DOWN, 0.50 to 0.45, not up. There is no sub-population argument anywhere in this estimate that resolves into a confidence number. Two conditions make that structural rather than a promise: the sub-population disclosure is filed as a condition, and the class-splitting escape is refused in writing RAW FIGURE PROMOTED TO A FIELD AFTER THE FACT, and this is the one edit made to this record after the work began, so it is stated plainly. active_quantity (3.6h) is unchanged and is what was predicted. raw_active_quantity (6.5h) records the uncorrected bottom-up figure the correction was applied to, which this note already stated in prose. It was promoted because closing OUT-0009 showed ScoringAgent's prequential walk assumes every row is uncorrected -- its question is whether applying the correction would have helped -- so reading 3.6h as raw made it apply the factor twice and report the correction as harmful. Nothing about the prediction changed; a number that existed only in prose became one a backtest can read.
risk_note: Four risks, and for the first time the largest one is that the correction itself is wrong. FIRST: 3.6h is a corrected number carrying a factor whose confidence is 0.3875 - a coin-flip-grade signal by construction, since n/(n+5) caps the sample term at exactly one half at the threshold. If Phase 8 comes in near 6.5h, the raw estimate was right and the correction was the error, and that is a MORE interesting outcome for the Phase 12 demo than another uncorrected miss would have been. This risk is accepted deliberately and is the point of applying the factor rather than admiring it. SECOND: cross-document outcome matching is the one item with an invariant standing against it. ADR 0015's single-document offering is load-bearing for the whole citation gate, and if the cross-document case cannot be built without widening the offering, the right answer is to cut the item, not the invariant - and cutting it mid-phase costs the time already spent discovering that. THIRD: the FusionBridge determinism question is priced as a possibility and not as a plan. If recognition turns out to need a model after all, the phase gains a prompt, a prompt version, a citation path and a set of refusals that this estimate has priced at roughly half strength. FOURTH, and the one every phase underestimates: the finding that fires only on a FLIP. The interesting output is not 'here is a calibrated number' but 'this calibrated number changes the answer', which means the code has to evaluate the predicate twice and compare two three-valued verdicts where UNKNOWN is not FALSE. A raw TRUE going to a calibrated UNKNOWN is not a breach and must not read as one. That comparison is small, arithmetic, and exactly the kind of thing that has consumed a day in each of the last four phases. Not on the list: the line count

conditions: NO NEW STORAGE IS ADDED FOR THE CHALLENGE, and this was verified against praxis/domain/records.py:442 before the estimate was written rather than assumed. That argument goes in the ADR, not in a comment

Confidence rose 0.3875 to 0.4329 because n rose five to six, which is n/(n+5) doing exactly what ADR 0024 designed it to do and is not new information about the estimator. THE ARITHMETIC, both steps kept separate on purpose. Step one, the RAW estimate: built bottom-up from the line items in conditions by the same procedure the six fitted estimates used - three agents at roughly 300/320/220 production lines, a store pass at 300, a CLI at 200, an eval module plus edits at 250, tests at least as large throughout, four ADRs, a corpus extension and the report - which lands at 6.5h, the same figure EST-0009 reached for a phase of comparable shape. Phase 9 has one more ADR than Phase 8 and one fewer genuinely risky item, since nothing here fights an existing invariant the way cross-document matching fought ADR 0015. Those roughly cancel and the raw figure is left where the procedure put it. The procedure was deliberately NOT made more pessimistic first: the factor corrects this procedure, so adjusting the procedure and then applying the correction would count the same adjustment twice. Step two, the CORRECTION: 6.5 x 0.5527 = 3.5926, logged as 3.6h. The band travels with it, which ADR 0024 made inseparable for exactly this reason: 6.5 x 0.7169 = 4.66h at the least-corrected end and 6.5 x 0.4261 = 2.77h at the most-corrected end, so the honest statement is 3.6h with a plausible range of 2.8h to 4.7h. The six actuals this was fitted on are 4.2, 2.75, 4.6, 2.8, 2.1 and 3.5, arithmetic mean 3.33h, which puts 3.6h just above the historical mean where a phase of this scope belongs. WHY THE CONFIDENCE DOES NOT MOVE, stated because it is the number most tempting to raise. OUT-0009 was the first exact match in this project's history and the first correction that worked, and it is extremely tempting to read that as the method being proven. It is n=1. One estimate landing on the nose after a correction is equally consistent with a lucky raw estimate and an offsetting error, and OUT-0009's own notes say so. Raising confidence here on the strength of one result would be EST-0008's mistake with the sign flipped - moving the confidence lever to express something that is not a confidence - so confidence stays at 0.45, exactly where EST-0009 put it, and the entire content of this estimate remains in the QUANTITY. WHETHER THE CLASSIFICATION IS HONEST, answered rather than dodged for the second phase running. This phase mixes one LLM-reasoning component with two likely-deterministic ones, and the question is whether that makes it something other than agent-implementation. It does not. The class is defined by the shape of the work - agents built into this codebase's spine plus a store pass, a CLI and a quarter of the metrics table - and not by how many of the components call a model. The fitted population already spans the full range internally: Phase 7 called no model at all and produced the worst ratio in the sample at 2.62x, Phase 5 called five and produced 1.41x, and there is no monotone relationship between model-callingness and the ratio anywhere in the six. Phase 9 at two deterministic and one model-calling sits inside that population rather than at its edge, which makes the factor applicable on the same grounds EST-0009 used. The alternative - splitting agent-implementation so Phase 9 is compared only against mixed phases - would drop every resulting sub-class below n=5 and silence BiasDetective entirely, and inventing a class boundary to escape a factor is the override ADR 0024 refuses to provide arriving through a side door. The class stays; the concern is logged as a condition.
risk_note: Four risks, and the largest is a number this phase cannot control. FIRST: the concede rate is the one metric here whose offline value is meaningless and whose bounds are real. The product owner set 5 per cent and 60 per cent as the marks of a broken agent, and against the mock the number will be a property of _TRUE_BIAS = 0.7 rather than of any reasoning. There is no way to earn a trustworthy concede rate offline, so the phase ships the measurement, states plainly whose number it is, and reports whichever value comes out without tuning the corpus to move it. Being unable to answer the question the metric exists for is itself the finding. SECOND: CuratorAgent writes RETRACTIONS, which is the most destructive-looking thing any agent in this system has done, even though retraction is a new version rather than a delete. A curator that merges two assumptions which merely look alike withdraws a live belief, and the blast radius is a decision losing the assumption underneath it. The refusals are the whole defence and they are priced inside the component; the specific one to get right is refusing to retire anything a live Decision assumes. THIRD: the contradicts-implies-supersedes merge rule is a RULE and it can be wrong. Two assumptions that genuinely conflict are not always a revision of one another, and the corpus's revision notes are the friendly case rather than the general one. It is priced with an explicit ADR assumption written to expire rather than as a silent heuristic. FOURTH, and the one every phase underestimates: the challenger writes onto a record whose validator refuses a verdict with no challenge, so every path that records a verdict must record the prose that produced it, including the paths where the model answered badly. That is small, arithmetic and exactly the kind of thing that has consumed a day in each of the last five phases. Not on the list: the line count.
blocked_note: 6.0h, and for the sixth time this is the least meaningful number in the record. Blocked has now been predicted six times and missed six times, in both directions and by wide margins: 20.0 against 12.8, 16.0 against 72.3, 24.0 against 17.3, 18.0 against 0.9, 18.0 against 2.0, and 12.0 against 0.1. For this project blocked time is elapsed wall clock between sessions ended by credit exhaustion, so it contains nights: it measures when the author sleeps, not when the work waits. It is logged because the record has the field and a hole is worse than a bad number, and the figure moves from 12.0 to 6.0 only because the geometric mean of the nine actuals is 5.79h - not because anything about Phase 9 predicts it. NO calibration factor is applied and none could be: BiasDetective's ratios are computed on active quantities only, so there is no fitted factor for blocked time and manufacturing one from nine points that measure a sleep schedule would be arithmetic dressed as a prediction. Compare active against active.

subject: Phase 10 - THE EVALUATION HARNESS, the phase in which the project's metrics claims stop being assembled by hand and become one re-runnable command: the corpus grown past 60 documents with clean controls, all-adversarial memos and orphan assumptions added to what Phases 3-9 already planted; a coherently-citing mock mode so the offline table has numbers in it rather than correct zeros; the three metrics the original brief named that do not yet exist (calibration MAE improvement, abstention precision, and citation accuracy under its own name); a ten-rung ablation runner that executes a prefix of the pipeline and reports what each layer contributes; and praxis eval ablate rendering it. No new agents.
conditions: PRICED BY REFUSAL VOCABULARY AND INTEGRATION-POINT COUNT, NOT BY LINES, AND THIS IS THE DELIBERATE CHANGE THE PHASE 9 HANDOVER ASKED FOR. OUT-0010 was wrong in both directions at once: it over-estimated the hours and under-estimated the volume by about 40%, which means hours-per-line is what the fitted factor has actually been correcting and the line-count line item was carrying none of its own weight. So no line count is predicted here at all. The two quantities that are counted are SIXTEEN refusal paths and TWENTY integration points, enumerated below, at roughly 12 minutes per refusal path and 8 minutes per integration point.

THE SIXTEEN REFUSAL PATHS, counted because each is a place the work stops being typing and starts being thought. (1) A new topic whose reversal_predicate interval is not provably disjoint from its predicate plants a contradiction nothing can settle, so verify_corpus has to catch it rather than the corpus shipping broken. (2) A clean control document has zero ground truth items and _document_problems has never seen one. (3) counts() and _graded must not divide by zero on a document that contributes nothing. (4) GroundTruthItem's own validator refuses fields or links on a distractor, so an all-adversarial memo must plant none. (5) An orphan assumption has no assumes edge and _edge_problems must not require one. (6) A floor-only segmenter must report ZERO model calls, not one, or the cost column lies. (7) A coherently-citing mock shown a passage with no sentence long enough to quote must fall back rather than emit an empty quotation. (8) The same mock shown a prompt with no bracketed ordinals at all -- not every agent shows an offering -- must not crash. (9) The same mock with the flag off must be BYTE-IDENTICAL to today, because 2948 tests and nine phase reports rest on it. (10) MAE with zero scored rows must report not-measured, never 0.0000, which reads as perfect. (11) Abstention precision with zero abstentions must do the same, never 1.0. (12) An ablation rung whose predecessor produced nothing must refuse the rung rather than report a zero as a contribution. (13) Rung 0's counterfactual precision must refuse when its denominator is empty. (14, 15, 16) The CLI's three: unknown rung name, missing corpus, unwritable output path.

THE TWENTY INTEGRATION POINTS, and this is the axis on which Phase 10 is unlike every phase before it. Phases 3-9 each added new modules that mostly talked to themselves; this phase adds ONE new module (praxis/eval/ablation.py) and threads changes through code that nine phases already depend on. topics.py into _schedule, _revisable and world_assumption_key (1). templates.py's TEMPLATES tuple into _schedule's template_index arithmetic, which must not hand a control template a topic rotation (2). generator._write and DocumentGroundTruth for zero-item documents (1). verify_corpus's three problem-finders (3). cli.py's corpus generate reporting (1). SegmenterAgent into IngestionPipeline, already injectable and therefore the cheapest of the twenty (1). synthesis._Answerer into MockProvider into provider_for into cli_eval (3). eval/calibration.py's CalibrationScore into report.py's markdown AND its json (2). eval/governance.py's GovernanceScore into the same two (2). harness.evaluate decomposed so a prefix of it can run (1). ablation.py into report.py (1). cli_eval into cli.py (1). praxis doctor's NON_LLM_AGENTS list, because MAE and abstention precision are arithmetic and invariant 3 has to keep holding (1).

THE PHASE BELONGS IN agent-implementation AND THE DECISION IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN INHERITED. Phase 10 adds no agents at all, which is a real argument for a new class, and the argument is refused for a reason about the data rather than about convenience. The class already contains work of this shape: EST-0004 (Phase 3) was adapters and a block grid with no agent judgement in it, and EST-0008 (Phase 7) was the phase in which every component called no model at all. In practice agent-implementation has meant a Praxis build phase by this author in this codebase, and Phase 10 is one. Opening an eval-harness class would put this estimate at n=0, which discards the only calibration signal the project has in order to make a taxonomic point. If phases keep arriving that add no agents, the time to split the class is when the new one has five rows of its own and BiasDetective can speak about it -- not at the first instance, on one row.

SCOPE STATED IN ADVANCE, so the report can say whether it held. IN: eight new topics, three new document kinds, the segmenter floor flag, the coherent mock mode, three new metrics, the ablation runner and its renderer, praxis eval ablate, two ADRs. OUT and deferred with the reason changed rather than repeated: no orchestrator (ADR 0004 is still Phase 11's), no ReviewTriageAgent (deferred out of Phase 9 to Phase 11 and it stays there), no live-provider run of anything. Nothing here needs a credential and nothing here will acquire one.

THE CITATION GATE IS NOT DISABLED FOR THE ABLATION, and this is the one design decision in the phase that could have gone the lazy way. A rung that turns the gate off would write span_ids that do not contain their claims, which is invariant 6 and its 'no exceptions for convenience' clause read literally. The gate's contribution is computed counterfactually from the refusal record instead: a refused claim has no valid span, so it can pair with no key item under the span-overlap rule, so gate-off precision is exactly TP/(TP+FP+refused). That is arithmetic on numbers the harness already collects, it is deterministic, and it costs one refusal path (13 above) rather than four agent constructor changes.
calibration_note: Corrected ONCE, per the rule EST-0009 established and OUT-0010 tempted the project to break. BiasDetective was re-run over docs/dogfood/ rather than copied from the handover table, and agrees with it: agent-implementation at n=7 is 1.9670x over, factor 0.5084, band 0.3674-0.7034 (1.42x-2.72x over), confidence 0.4404. Raw bottom-up 6.0h x 0.5084 = 3.05h, logged as 3.1h. OUT-0010 came in 1.8000x over a corrected estimate, which is exactly the shape that argues for applying the factor a second time, and the second application is REFUSED. One row is not a trend; the prequential walk is what answers the question and it says the correction helped on both rows it grades and worsened neither. If corrected figures keep landing near 1.8x over, the honest response is that the FACTOR is too small -- and it moves on its own as the sample grows, from 0.5527 at n=6 to 0.5084 at n=7 -- not that the procedure needs two passes.
risk_note: THE ONE THING THAT COULD MAKE THIS PHASE MUCH LONGER IS THE COHERENT MOCK, and it is priced as three refusal paths and three integration points rather than as a rewrite because it is genuinely one function: pick the ordinal first, then quote from that ordinal's passage instead of from the whole prompt. The risk is not writing it, it is BLAST RADIUS -- if the default draw shifts by one call the seeded generator moves and an unknown number of the 2948 tests change their expected numbers. The defence is that the mode is opt-in and the default path is untouched, and the specific thing to get right is refusal path 9: byte-identical with the flag off. SECOND RISK: harness.evaluate currently runs its stages as one straight-line function with comments explaining why three of them cannot move. Decomposing it so a prefix can run must preserve that ordering exactly, and the ordering constraints are real -- fusion needs calibration's factors, governance needs every stage's findings. A rung ladder that silently reordered them would produce a table that is wrong in a way no test would catch. THIRD, and the one every phase underestimates: the corpus verifies against itself before it is written, so every one of the eight new topics needs a predicate and a reversal predicate whose intervals are provably disjoint, and that is eight small pieces of interval arithmetic done by hand. Not on the list, deliberately: the line count.
blocked_note: 3.9h, and for the seventh time this is the least meaningful number in the record. Blocked has now been predicted seven times and missed seven times, in both directions and by wide margins. For this project blocked time is elapsed wall clock between sessions ended by credit exhaustion, so it contains nights: it measures when the author sleeps, not when the work waits. It is logged because the record has the field and a hole is worse than a bad number. The figure is the geometric mean of all ten actuals (1.52, 68.5, 24.4, 12.8, 72.3, 17.3, 0.9, 2.0, 0.1, 0.1), which is 3.859h, and it moves from 6.0 only because that mean moved. NO calibration factor is applied and none could be: BiasDetective's ratios are computed on active quantities only, so there is no fitted factor for blocked time. Compare active against active.

subject: Phase 11 - DASHBOARD, DEMO AND LANDING PAGE, the phase that makes Phases 1-10 visible to someone who has never read a line of the code: a standalone landing page built to a provided visual spec; a read-only FastAPI layer over the existing store reads; a single-page dashboard with a timeline, a decision drill-down carrying the full argument chain, the Fusion finding rendered as a provenance strip, calibration charts per person and per work class, the review queue, and a panel exposing Phase 2's trace store; and a scripted demo dataset seeded from Praxis's own committed history. The landing page is a scope addition beyond the original Phase 11 brief, made at the product owner's direction with design assets provided.
conditions: PRICED BY RENDER TARGETS AND STORE READS, NOT BY LINES AND NOT BY REFUSAL PATHS. EST-0011 priced by refusal-vocabulary size (16 paths) and integration points (20), and OUT-0011 vindicated that unit at 1.1613x - the closest this estimator has come. But a refusal path is a place where code must decline to answer, and that is a property of agent work. This phase has no refusal vocabulary: a panel that renders wrongly is not a refusal, it is a mismatch against a picture. Inheriting the unit because it worked last time would be as unprincipled as inheriting lines. Lines are excluded outright - OUT-0010 was wrong on hours and volume in opposite directions at once, and the brief for this phase names that as settled in both directions.

TERM 1 - EIGHTEEN RENDER TARGETS at roughly 15 minutes each, 4.5h. A render target is a distinct visual component in the provided assets, counted rather than a screen, because a screen is a container and prices a list and an SVG layout engine identically. Landing: (1) nav bar, (2) hero headline and CTAs, (3) the offset product shot, (4) the offline-first / append-only / deterministic trust row, (5) the three feature cards with sparkline art. Shell: (6) the left rail, (7) the header with status chips, (8) the KPI card. Views: (9) the decision dependency graph, (10) assumption health, (11) the calibration lens with its two overlaid curves, (12) the collateral-impact callout, (13) the append-only audit rail, (14) the review queue, (15) the decision drill-down argument chain, (16) calibration charts per person and per class, (17) the timeline view, (18) the reasoning panel over the trace store.

TERM 2 - NINE NEW STORE READS at roughly 12 minutes each, 1.8h. Each is SQL plus a frozen dataclass plus tests, added to praxis/store/reports.py beside calibration_history rather than inline in a route handler: audit_timeline, decision_index, decision_detail, finding_queue, findings_for, calibration_groups, assumption_health, estimate_detail, trace_index. This is the integration-point analogue and it is where the correctness risk actually sits, because the schema is append-only and a read that forgets to filter to the current version silently double-counts history.

TERM 3 - EIGHT WEB PLUMBING POINTS at roughly 8 minutes each, 1.1h: the FastAPI app, the route module, the response models, praxis serve, praxis demo seed, ADR 0036, ADR 0037, and the deliberate widening of tests/test_boundaries.py.

TERM 4 - THE DESIGN-FIDELITY LOOP, 1.1h, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS UNIT IS NEW RATHER THAN A RESKIN OF THE OLD ONE. In every phase so far correctness was binary: the predicate parses or it does not, the citation gate refuses or it does not, the test is green or it is red. Here the acceptance test is whether the built page looks like the provided picture, which is a comparison loop with no green tick terminating it. Pricing that at zero is the standard way frontend estimates go wrong, so it is a line item rather than an omission. It is also the term I have the least basis for, and it is the first place to look if this estimate misses.
RAW BOTTOM-UP TOTAL 8.5h ACTIVE, uncorrected, for the reason in calibration_note.

BLOCKED 4.2h is the geometric mean of all eleven recorded blocked actuals (computed: 4.1505), not an engineering prediction. Its known weakness is stated rather than padded away: EST-0011 predicted 3.9h on this same basis and OUT-0011 recorded 8.6h, essentially all of it one hard session limit. A session interruption is still not in this distribution and this figure does not attempt to price one.

ASSUMES the frontend needs no build step, no npm and no CDN - forced by invariant 1 and offline-first, since a CDN script tag means the dashboard renders blank without a network. If a build toolchain turns out to be unavoidable, this estimate is void rather than merely wrong.

Checked before estimating: offline the citation gate refuses 38 of 40 claims so one estimate reaches the store, no calibration group could reach MINIMUM_SAMPLE even fully populated, and fusion recall is 0 of 3. That corpus grades extraction; it does not populate a dashboard.
calibration_note: NO CORRECTION APPLIED, AND n IS ZERO RATHER THAN SMALL. This is the first estimate this project has ever logged in the frontend work class. The dogfood corpus holds exactly four classes - scaffolding (n=1), data-modelling (n=1), llm-integration (n=1) and agent-implementation (n=8) - and frontend is in none of them. The only frontend rows anywhere in the repository are in the synthetic corpus under .praxis-tmp/, which is untracked generator output about fictional estimators and is not this estimator's calibration data. So there is no factor, no band and no confidence to apply: BiasDetective refuses below MINIMUM_SAMPLE=5 and it would refuse this at n=0. agent-implementation's fitted 0.6534 factor is deliberately NOT borrowed. EST-0002 faced this exact situation and wrote down the reason - applying another class's correction here would be the unprincipled adjustment this product exists to replace - and that sentence still applies. The stated confidence of 0.35 is below EST-0011's 0.42 for the same reason: there is no prior in this class at all.
